meta.title: Eternity's Reach — Kingshot 777
meta.description: Kingshot Eternity's Reach guide: the RRLLR skill order, march distribution by phase, the Skill 3 recall loop, Vein Outburst timing, and Governor Charm planning.

tldr.heading: TL;DR
items: Rush Skill 3. The whole run is built around unlocking the vein-capture passive as fast as possible — it pays 5,000 copper every time a march reaches a new vein.
Recommended skill order is RRLLR: Cesare copper → march speed → Skill 3 vein bonus → copper efficiency → gathering burst. Skip the combat branches unless you're a top player.
Marches are never idle. Weak marches farm Cesares (no troop loss, no healing); strong marches run the Send → wait 60s → recall → re-send loop to trigger Skill 3.
Save Skill 5 for Vein Outbursts, and stop attacking Cesares once everything is maxed — full-node gathering out-scores combat late.

overview.heading: What Eternity's Reach is
items: A timed copper-ore event built around movement efficiency: rotate marches, use the event skill tree well, and react to high-value spawns (Cesares and fractured veins).
Cesares are safe PvE guards — they cause no troop loss, so you never need to heal after hitting them.
Copper ore feeds Governor Charm materials, which unlock at Town Center 25. Even below TC25 the rewards are worth banking for later.
Passive sitters lose. The top boards belong to players who keep every march slot busy for the whole window.

skillOrder.heading: Skill order — RRLLR
skillOrder.intro: Skill order is the single most important decision in the event. Rushing Skill 3 defines your entire run.

rows.effect: IMPORTANT — 5,000 copper when you occupy a common vein (1-minute cooldown). This passive is the engine of the whole event.
Troop gathering speed +50% for 60s after activation (only for troops deployed while it's active). Save it for Vein Outbursts.

skillOrder.note: The other branches focus on combat and are strongly discouraged unless you're among the top players.

rows.whatToDo: Chain-attack untargeted Cesares to level fast. Ignore gathering entirely until Skill 3 unlocks.
Run the recall loop below. This is where most points — and most mistakes — happen.

rows.marches: All marches → gather during a burst
rows.whatToDo: Treat Skill 5 as a 1-minute multiplier; between bursts return to the 2 / 3–4 split.
Stop attacking Cesares. Hold ~6 active nodes and rotate. Gathering now out-scores combat.

skill3Loop.heading: The Skill 3 recall loop (core mechanic)
skill3Loop.intro: Skill 3 pays a points bonus every time a march reaches a vein — you're not gathering for the resources, you're gathering to trigger the bonus.
items: Send a gathering march to a nearby vein and note when the 5,000-ore bonus lands.
Wait ~60 seconds (account for the march time to your closest vein).
Recall the march manually, then re-send it immediately.
Send → wait 60s → recall → re-send, repeated non-stop. Each recall costs nothing and re-triggers the passive.

skill5.heading: Vein Outbursts & Skill 5
items: Never auto-fire Skill 5 — use it only during a Vein Outburst.
While Skill 5 is active: send ALL marches to gather and let the full minute run — do not recall early.
While inactive: 1–2 marches on Cesares, 3–4 on veins, recalling every ~1 minute to keep Skill 3 flowing.
Skill 5 has a cooldown, so firing it early wastes a full burst.

positioning.heading: Positioning & teleports
items: When you get a free or advanced teleport, jump to a spot where two or three veins sit close together for short march times.
Put your town center beside a cluster of veins so the recall loop cycles faster.
If a whale is camping you or the area is crowded, use the "scorched earth" move: teleport to a quiet corner and keep farming instead of fighting.

charms.heading: Governor Charm planning
items: Copper ore and event rewards feed Governor Charm materials — Charm Designs and Charm Guides become bottlenecks later.
Governor Charms unlock at Town Center 25; below that, still bank the materials for future planning.
Check a charm database or calculator before spending materials unevenly across charms.

commonMistakes.heading: Common mistakes that kill scores
items: Fighting for the center — it looks prestigious but is mathematically inefficient.
Engaging in PvP — a loss puts your heroes on a cooldown timer.
Letting marches sit idle — idle marches are lost ore.
Using Skill 5 at random instead of saving it for Vein Outbursts.
Over-farming Cesares late game when full-node gathering scores more.
Note: veins auto-collect and still count at the timer's end, so you don't have to recall them before the event closes.

mapElements.alt: A Cesare guard, a common vein, and a fractured vein on the event map
mapElements.caption: Your two target types: Cesares (safe PvE copper, no troop loss) and veins (where Skill 3 pays out).

skillTree.alt: Eternity's Reach event skill tree showing the left and right option at each of the five levels
skillTree.caption: The event skill tree. RRLLR = right, right, left, left, right — note Skill 3 (left) is the 5,000-copper vein passive.

peak.alt: The Peak of Eternity structure at the center of the battlefield
peak.caption: The Peak of Eternity unlocks ~23 minutes into the battle and rewards copper for time held — prestigious, but usually less efficient than cycling veins.
